The four S1 body-part columns overlap (the vibrissae lie within the rostrum) and do not cover all of S1, so they must not be summed: their printed percentages sum to 107, 108 and 104% of S1 for cases 9213, 9321 and 9324 (area ratios 107.1, 108.0 and 103.4%); without the vibrissae they cover 89-96% of S1. The build records these per-case sums in table_checks as not evaluable: there is no total of 100 to test.

The build re-runs 55 relations into table_checks: Tot. SS = S1 + S2 (4); percentage = 100 x area / base, each also compared with the printed value at its printed precision (18); S1 % + S2 % = 100 (4); the body-part percentages summed per case (3, recorded as not evaluable, see Method:not_additive); Average = mean and sample SD (n - 1) of the cases for every area (14) and percentage (12) column. Tolerance = only what rounding of the printed cells can explain. Result (Python mirror; R NOT RUN): 52 pass, 0 mismatch, 3 not evaluable. All the checks that pass but one reproduce the printed value exactly at its printed precision; the exception is the HL/trunk percentage SD (see HL/trunk %).
